stops.note: rest, repose, giving rise to quiescere (to become quiet, to rest)
to find rest in, to comply, from ad- and quiescere
stops.meaning: to find rest in, to comply

stops.note: first recorded in 1613 in the writing of the Scottish churchman Patrick Forbes, by way of French 'acquiescer'
stops.meaning: to accept something without protest, though not enthusiastically

current_meaning: to accept or comply with something without protest, though not necessarily with enthusiasm
